This page gets you from *no R installed* to *the first course example running*.
Four steps, about 15–20 minutes, most of it downloading. Do this **before** the
workshop; the course itself does not wait for installation.

**Stuck on a work laptop with no admin rights or a blocked proxy?** Skip to the
[hosted fallback](#hosted-fallback) — nothing to install.

**Already have R 4.4 or newer and RStudio?** Skip to
[Get the course project](#get-the-course-project).

## 1. Install R and RStudio :arrow_double_down: {.smaller}

Go to the Posit download page: <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>

It links the matching **R installer** for your platform and the **RStudio
installer**. Install R first, then RStudio, accepting the defaults.

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Windows

Run the R installer, then the RStudio installer. No other choices are needed.

## macOS

Open the R `.pkg`, then the RStudio `.dmg`. The installers detect Intel vs.
Apple silicon — you do not need to choose.

## Linux

Posit provides Ubuntu/Debian and RHEL/Fedora builds on the same page. On
Ubuntu/Debian, open the downloaded `.deb` with the graphical package installer.
Other distributions: ask the organizers before the day.
:::

**Check it worked.** Open RStudio, click in the **Console** (left pane, not the
Terminal tab), and run:

```r
getRversion()
```

Any version **4.4 or newer** is fine. The course was built with R 4.5.

## 2. Get the course project :inbox_tray: {.smaller}

Everything for the course ships as one project folder. Two ways to get it —
pick one:

- **Git users:** `git clone https://github.com/saumil-sh/SC09-RISW26`
- **Everyone else:** download `https://github.com/saumil-sh/SC09-RISW26/archive/refs/heads/main.zip` in your browser and
  extract it somewhere normal — Desktop or your home folder. (Double-click the
  ZIP on Windows/macOS; `unzip` on Linux.) **Not** a temporary folder: your
  edits must survive the day. No Git or GitHub account needed. The ZIP
  extracts to a folder named **`SC09-RISW26-main`** — open that folder, not
  its parent.

Either way: open the folder and double-click **`SC09-RISW26.Rproj`**. RStudio
opens the project, sets the working directory, and activates the package
environment automatically.

If a folder from an earlier attempt already exists, open it and continue — do
not delete it; your work is inside.

*Console alternative:*

```r
install.packages("usethis")
usethis::use_course("https://github.com/saumil-sh/SC09-RISW26/archive/refs/heads/main.zip")
```

## 3. Restore the packages :package: {.smaller}

The course pins exact package versions so your results match the slides. Still
in the project's **Console**:

```r
install.packages("renv")
renv::restore()
```

First run downloads and installs the packages (a few minutes). If it asks
whether to proceed, answer `y`.

Notes:

- `renv::restore()` installs **R packages** — not R, not RStudio, not system
  libraries.
- A message that *"the project was last used with a different R version"* is a
  warning, not a failure, as long as your R is 4.4+.
- If a package must be compiled from source: install
  [Rtools45](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/rtools45/rtools.html)
  on Windows; Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`) on macOS;
  standard build tools on Linux. Then rerun `renv::restore()`.

## 4. Confirm the example runs :white_check_mark:

```r
packageVersion("rxsim")     # expect 0.3.0
source("R/part-2/1-one-arm.R")
print(results)
```

You should see **one row** of results — 100 patients, `mean_y` near 0.44,
`sd_y` near 1. If so, you are ready for the workshop.

## Coming back later :back:

Reopen `SC09-RISW26.Rproj` and run whichever script you like. Downloading and
`renv::restore()` are one-time setup.

## Hosted fallback :cloud: {.smaller}

If your machine cannot install software or reach CRAN, run the course on
[Posit Cloud](https://posit.cloud/) — RStudio in your browser, nothing to
install. The free tier is enough for the workshop day.

1. Go to <https://posit.cloud/> and sign up (free) or log in.
2. Click **New Project → New Project from a Git Repository** and paste
   `https://github.com/saumil-sh/SC09-RISW26`.
3. Wait for the project to open, then run the same two lines as everyone
   else in the Console:

```r
install.packages("renv")
renv::restore()
source("R/part-2/1-one-arm.R")
```

`renv::restore()` installs the pinned packages into the cloud project (a few
minutes, first time only). One row of results and you are ready.

*No Git?* In step 2, choose **New Project → Empty Project** instead. In the
**Files** pane (bottom-right), click **Upload**, upload the course ZIP from
`https://github.com/saumil-sh/SC09-RISW26/archive/refs/heads/main.zip`, and tick the option to expand it. Then continue
with step 3.

Your cloud project persists — you can come back to it after the workshop.

## Troubleshooting :wrench: {.smaller}

- **Console vs. terminal.** Commands shown in `r` blocks go in the RStudio
  **Console**. You never need the system terminal on the happy path.
- **Keep the first error message.** It is the useful one. Do not work around an
  error by installing newer package versions — that breaks the pinned
  environment. Ask an instructor or the course contact instead.
- **A parallel example left your session stuck?** Run
  `future::plan(future::sequential)` to release the background workers.
- **Corporate proxy / no admin rights.** Not fixable in the room — use the
  [hosted fallback](#hosted-fallback) and talk to your IT later.
- **Quarto is optional.** Participants only need R to run the scripts and a
  browser to view the slides. RStudio 2022.07.1 and later bundles Quarto for
  anyone who wants to re-render the slides.
